empty: No Compose project found in this node's projects folder.
pickOne: Choose a file to read or edit it.
run.title: Run {{project}}
new.title: New project
new.name: Project name
new.envHint: The .env stays on the node (private file, never shown again here). Leave it empty if the project needs none. Nothing is started: deploy from the project page.
new.tip: Creates a project folder with its compose file. Nothing runs until you deploy it.
new.nameTip: Becomes the folder name on the node and the Compose project name. Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.
new.envTip: Optional private values (passwords, keys). Never shown again in the audit log, only the variable names.
run.tip.up: Creates and starts the services (docker compose up -d)
run.tip.down: Stops and removes the containers. Volumes are kept.
run.tip.stop: Stops the services without removing them
run.tip.pull: Downloads newer images; does not restart anything
run.tip.build: Builds the images from the project's Dockerfiles
run.downConfirm: Bring {{project}} down? Its containers are removed (volumes are kept) and its sites go offline.
views.title: Projects by state
emptyWithFound: No project is managed yet. {{count}} folder(s) found on the node can be imported: see “To import”.
discovered.explain: Folders of the node that hold a Compose file. Nothing is read or changed until you import them.
discovered.none: Nothing to import: every folder with a Compose file is already managed or ignored.
discovered.name: Project
discovered.labelsTip: Short words to sort your projects, separated by commas. They apply to every project you import now.
discovered.ignoreTip: Hides these folders from this list. You can bring them back from “Ignored”.
discovered.safe: Importing or ignoring never changes the folder or its containers: running containers are simply picked up as they are.
ignored.explain: Folders you set aside. Restore one to see it in “To import” again.
unmanage.tip: Takes the project out of Armadok. The folder and its containers are left alone.
unmanage.confirm: Stop managing {{project}}? Its folder and containers stay as they are; you can import it again later.
